title: test(plugin-grid,console): pin the members of object-grid's three source-and-destination keys (objectui#8071 slice 14)
body:
Part of objectui#8071 — slice 14 of the block card. Refs: objectui#8071.

Three `object-grid` keys move from `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTIONS` into `MEMBER_PINS`:
**`aggregations`**, **`dataSource`**, **`navigation`**. Each gets a pin that
constrains what the RENDERER reads, not what the registration declares.

Clause-②: no — this slice pins existing behaviour and changes no declaration surface.

## Merge base and the ledger readings, re-taken here

Branched from `origin/main` = `19d1f24bfb2a416e1299072d9245d0682d98f801`, which is
also the merge base (`git merge-base HEAD origin/main`). The ledger was re-counted at
that base with a depth-aware, comment-and-string-aware direct-key counter; its
"non-property tokens at depth 0" bucket read `[]` on every record before and after, so
the parse is clean and the counts are readings.

| quantity | at the merge base | after this change |
|---|---|---|
| `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTIONS` direct keys | 16 | 13 |
| `MEMBER_PINS` direct keys | 75 | 78 |
| `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTION_CEILING` | 16 | 13 |

**I moved these three keys from exemptions to pins**, and nothing else moved in either
direction — the set leaving exemptions and the set entering pins are the same set,
computed and compared rather than asserted:

- left `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTIONS`: `object-grid.aggregations`, `object-grid.dataSource`, `object-grid.navigation`
- entered `MEMBER_PINS`: `object-grid.aggregations`, `object-grid.dataSource`, `object-grid.navigation`
- entered exemptions: none · left pins: none

## Why three, and not the seven the block had left

Slice 12's dev measured `columns`, `filter`, `grouping` and `sort` as one slice EACH and
refused a batch containing them; slice 14's dispatch adopted that refusal. The three
taken here are what remains once those four are set aside, and they cluster: each names
a place outside the block's own rows — where the rows come from (`dataSource`), what a
roll-up is computed over once they are grouped (`aggregations`), and where a click goes
(`navigation`). None is read anywhere near the `dataTableSchema` fold slice 13 worked in.

I did **not** re-verify slice 12's four-key reading, and I did not touch any of those
four keys.

## What each pin constrains

**`object-grid.aggregations`** — new file
`packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/gridAggregationMembers-8071.test.tsx`. The two
members of one roll-up entry (`field`, `type`) read at the group header the grid paints.
The six `type` values do not agree about what `field` means: `count` never reads it
(it answers `rows.length`, including rows carrying no such cell) while `count_distinct`
does and skips the empties, asserted on the same group. Three silent arithmetic rules:
coercion is `Number()`, so an explicit `null` cell is a real ZERO that lowers `avg` and
WINS `min` while an ABSENT cell is `NaN` and is dropped; `avg` divides by the coerced
list, not the group (`count: 3` beside `avg: 5.50` in one header); and `min`/`max` over
no numeric cell report `0` rather than the `Infinity` a bare spread would put on screen.
Plus the formatting branches and the key's own presence rule — `aggregations` without
`grouping` computes and renders nothing, and an empty array is indistinguishable from an
absent key.

**`object-grid.dataSource`** — pre-existing file
`packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/ObjectGrid.elementDataSource.test.tsx`, read end to
end and GROWN. Its four existing cases cover `object`, `view` and `filter`; what they
could not state is the precedence the remaining members are read through. The rule now
pinned, in one sentence: a binding member beats the block's own key, and the block's own
key beats the view the binding named. Each member is a PAIR — binding `sort` overrides an
authored `sort` while a view's sort loses to it; binding `limit` overrides an authored
`pagination.pageSize` while a view's page size loses to it — because either half alone is
consistent with a renderer that just takes the last writer. The limit row also pins that
the cap is written into a COPY of the authored `pagination` object, so a sibling
`pageSizeOptions` survives: assigning a fresh single-key object would pass every `$top`
assertion and silently delete the rows-per-page list the author configured.

**`object-grid.navigation`** — new file
`packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/gridNavigationMembers-8071.test.tsx`. All six members
of the spec's strict `NavigationConfigSchema` (`mode`, `view`, `preventNavigation`,
`openNewTab`, `size`, `width`) through a real row click on the real grid, where the
registration names only `mode`. `preventNavigation` outranks every mode including the
overlay ones, with the same config minus the flag as the live control; `openNewTab`
outranks `mode: 'page'` and DISCARDS `view` on the way past; `view` is pinned as what it
is, the second argument handed to the host, with the literal fallback beside it; and
`size` / `width` are pinned as one decision with three outcomes read off the `--ov-w` the
shell publishes. Prior art stated rather than credited:
`ObjectGrid.overlayShellModes-9299.test.tsx` pins the four OVERLAY values of `mode` and
names no other member.

## Ablations — every pin, mutation proven on disk, restore proven by `git diff HEAD`

Each leg ran through `ablation-replace`, which counts the anchor before and after,
compares blob hashes, and refuses a mutation that did not move the file. Directions were
predicted before running and all three held.

| # | mutated | the "improvement" | predicted | observed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `packages/plugin-grid/src/useGroupedData.ts` | `count` reads the `field` member, as an author expects | red | **2 red**, 8 green |
| 2 | `packages/react/src/element-data-source/ElementDataSourceGate.tsx` | drop the `fromView` guard — last writer wins | red | **1 red**, 10 green |
| 3 | `packages/react/src/hooks/useNavigationOverlay.ts` | drop the `openNewTab` arm of the new-window test | red | **2 red**, 9 green |

Evidence, quoted from the tool:

- 1 — `anchor "return { field, type, value: rows.length };" x1 (before)` · `anchor x1 -> x0` · `ok mutation landed: anchor 1 -> 0, blob eeb8efc45f18 -> 772178738069` · red: *`type: count` IGNORES `field`* and *an ABSENT cell is dropped instead, so `avg` divides by the coerced list* · `ok restored: blob == HEAD (eeb8efc45f18) and git diff HEAD is empty`
- 2 — `ok mutation landed: anchor 1 -> 0, blob 7c8c8f7c115e -> ced2e08d7517` · red: *…but a VIEW's `sort` LOSES to the block's own `sort`* — and the binding-overrides row stayed GREEN, which is the pair working as designed: this mutation only reverses the view direction · `ok restored: blob == HEAD (7c8c8f7c115e)`
- 3 — `ok mutation landed: anchor 1 -> 0, blob 453569619892 -> ae9afb8baa73` · red: *`openNewTab` OUTRANKS `mode: "page"` and DISCARDS `view`* and *`openNewTab` with no `onNavigate` host opens the record URL directly* · `ok restored: blob == HEAD (453569619892)`

⚠️ **Ablation 2's first attempt was a NO-OP and is reported as one.** The replacement text
I first passed was a SUBSTRING of the anchor, so the tool read the replacement count as
`x1 -> x1` and refused: `the replacement count moved 1 -> 1, a rise of 0, not the
declared 1`. Nothing was measured on that attempt and the wrapped command never ran. The
second attempt used a textually distinct replacement and is the row above. This is the
same instrument trap this lane has paid for once before; the tool caught it, not me.

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/gridAggregationMembers-8071.test.tsx` — 10 passed
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/gridNavigationMembers-8071.test.tsx` — 11 passed
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/ObjectGrid.elementDataSource.test.tsx` — 11 passed (4 pre-existing + 7 added)
- `pnpm exec vitest run apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` — 199 passed
- `pnpm exec turbo run type-check --filter=@object-ui/plugin-grid --filter=@object-ui/console --concurrency=2` — 37 tasks successful (includes the dependency builds both projects resolve their `.d.ts` through)
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` — exit 0, one changeset with EMPTY frontmatter (test-only change, releases nothing)
- gates: `check:control-bytes`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:element-data-source-declaration` — all exit 0
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over all five changed paths — NOT GOVERNED, none of the five surfaces matched

## Acceptance notes

Noted, not filed:

- An aggregation chip prints its `type` member and never its `field` member, so two
  same-type roll-ups over different fields render as two chips reading the same word,
  told apart only by their values and their authored order. Pinned as current behaviour
  and written into the pin prose as a limit rather than frozen as a claim about what may
  never render. Who will meet this: whoever takes `object-grid.grouping` in a later
  slice, since it is the key that makes the header exist; **otherwise: no one**.

Scope kept: `object-grid.columns`, `filter`, `grouping` and `sort` are NOT addressed
here and remain open — slice 12 measured each as one slice on its own, and this PR
neither touches them nor re-measures them.
